# Recipe: fixed-origin development and attach

> **Local target only.** This page describes an explicitly owned development
> server. It is not a hosted deployment recipe.

Use this route when a test, browser shell, or native harness must keep one
backend origin stable while generated artifacts continue to change. Ordinary
`snapback dev` selects a free port. Its fixed profile keeps the same lifecycle
owner while pinning the backend port and declaring the separately owned client
origin.

## Run one fixed-profile development loop

For a Vite client on port 5173 and a backend pinned to 42080:

```sh
snapback dev snapback \
  --port 42080 \
  --external-client-origin http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

Snapback owns the backend child and generate/load watcher. It adds the declared
client origin to the exact development **request-body origin admission** used by
auth and other authority-bearing dev requests; `SNAPBACK_DEV_AUTH_ORIGINS` does
not define `/health` CORS, which is loopback-open and therefore is not evidence
that a client origin reached the admission set. Snapback does not launch or stop
the Vite process. Start that client with its own normal command in another
terminal.

The declared origin must equal the browser's actual Vite origin. A Vite server
bound as `127.0.0.1` is not the `localhost` origin even when both reach the same
machine. The authoritative receipt records the server's full normalized
admission set: the declared origins, valid ambient
`SNAPBACK_DEV_AUTH_ORIGINS`, and any provider-owned aliases.

Re-running the same command with `--attach` is idempotent only for the exact
intended lifecycle:

```sh
snapback dev snapback --attach \
  --port 42080 \
  --external-client-origin http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

Attach validates the host descriptor and live startup nonce, then compares the
owner-only receipt's application deployment, authority settlement, artifacts,
target profile, capability digest, actual client origins, app binding,
qualified native binary, and CLI wrapper with fresh live operational readiness
before it changes the listener. A stale listener or wrong binding refuses
without adopting, killing, or replacing the process. An expired binding on an
otherwise matching cut is reissued rather than treated as a foreign child.
Closing an attached handle never shuts down the original owner's child.
`SNAPBACK_DEV_FIXED_PORT_STALE_LISTENER` names an occupied port without the
intended receipt-bound lifecycle; `SNAPBACK_DEV_FIXED_BINDING_MISMATCH` names
a live lifecycle whose admitted binding facts differ from the request; and
`SNAPBACK_DEV_APPLICATION_READY_STALE` names a same-host receipt that differs
from live application or authority facts.

Do not infer readiness or origin from logs. The host descriptor names the
listener; its deterministic `<ready-file>.application-ready` sibling is the
authoritative `snapback.application-ready.v1` settlement and admission
receipt.

## Preserve the sessions startup carrier

The lifecycle owner writes the complete sessions startup carrier before first
bind and rewrites it on every successful regenerate before hot-load. An
additive successor preserves the database, accounts, custody, sessions, and
client stores while advancing the complete active deployment identity. The
event stream reports the old and new identities; continuity does not mean
identity equality. `dev-fresh` is the explicit destructive verb and is never
implied by regenerate or attach.

`snapback start --startup-artifacts ...` remains available for lower-level
diagnosis and lifecycle acceptance harnesses. It is not the application
authoring path and shifts carrier correctness and process ownership to the
caller.

## Bind a separately owned client honestly

For web, `@expo/snapback-vite` managed/auto mode invokes this same fixed
profile. Configure `setup.backendDirectory` and the plugin's backend `port`;
Vite pins its own loopback port with `strictPort`, declares that client origin,
and consumes the application receipt. `virtual:snapback/dev` projects the
receipt-issued binding through the same-origin relay. It does not manufacture
binding provenance or expose the private backend origin, receipt path, or
qualified-binary facts to browser code.

The default `SnapbackExpoProvider` is supervisor-owned. A raw `{ origin }` or
raw binding override is not a supported substitute for its admitted
environment and can refuse as binding unavailable or with
`SNAPBACK_APP_BINDING_OVERRIDE_UNCONFIRMED`. For a separately owned native
Expo process, the application shell must own a complete admitted
`SnapbackExpoEnvironmentV1` (binding plus authority/custody lifecycle), or use
the lower-level app client with that admitted binding. There is currently no
safe “just pass the fixed URL” shortcut.

The supervised Expo profile declares Metro's `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, and
`localhost` loopback aliases into `runDev` before backend start. The Rust
server's consumed dev-body origin set is therefore the set written to the
receipt. Expo keeps
its device-route binding in owner-only transient `expo-supervisor.json` and the
rendezvous response; it never writes that projection back into the
application-ready file. Those are inspection/admission projections; attach
still trusts the application receipt.

## Anti-patterns

- Starting a second public lifecycle with `snapback start` for ordinary app
  authoring.
- Running `--attach` without the exact live ready descriptor and database.
- Treating port occupancy as server identity or deleting a stale listener on
  attach refusal.
- Parsing server logs instead of consuming the host and application receipts.
- Passing a raw origin to `SnapbackExpoProvider` or weakening binding
  admission after an override refusal.
- Hand-editing `startup-artifacts.json`, binding environments, or `.env*`
  origins instead of declaring the fixed profile.

Use this route when a test, browser shell, or native harness must keep one
backend origin stable while generated artifacts continue to change. Ordinary
`snapback dev` selects a free port. Its fixed profile keeps the same lifecycle
owner while pinning the backend port and declaring the separately owned client
origin.

## Run one fixed-profile development loop

For a Vite client on port 5173 and a backend pinned to 42080:

```sh
snapback dev snapback \
  --port 42080 \
  --external-client-origin http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

Snapback owns the backend child and generate/load watcher. It adds the declared
client origin to the exact development **request-body origin admission** used by
auth and other authority-bearing dev requests; `SNAPBACK_DEV_AUTH_ORIGINS` does
not define `/health` CORS, which is loopback-open and therefore is not evidence
that a client origin reached the admission set. Snapback does not launch or stop
the Vite process. Start that client with its own normal command in another
terminal.

The declared origin must equal the browser's actual Vite origin. A Vite server
bound as `127.0.0.1` is not the `localhost` origin even when both reach the same
machine. The authoritative receipt records the server's full normalized
admission set: the declared origins, valid ambient
`SNAPBACK_DEV_AUTH_ORIGINS`, and any provider-owned aliases.

Re-running the same command with `--attach` is idempotent only for the exact
intended lifecycle:

```sh
snapback dev snapback --attach \
  --port 42080 \
  --external-client-origin http://127.0.0.1:5173
```

Attach validates the host descriptor and live startup nonce, then compares the
owner-only receipt's application deployment, authority settlement, artifacts,
target profile, capability digest, actual client origins, app binding,
qualified native binary, and CLI wrapper with fresh live operational readiness
before it changes the listener. A stale listener or wrong binding refuses
without adopting, killing, or replacing the process. An expired binding on an
otherwise matching cut is reissued rather than treated as a foreign child.
Closing an attached handle never shuts down the original owner's child.
`SNAPBACK_DEV_FIXED_PORT_STALE_LISTENER` names an occupied port without the
intended receipt-bound lifecycle; `SNAPBACK_DEV_FIXED_BINDING_MISMATCH` names
a live lifecycle whose admitted binding facts differ from the request; and
`SNAPBACK_DEV_APPLICATION_READY_STALE` names a same-host receipt that differs
from live application or authority facts.

Do not infer readiness or origin from logs. The host descriptor names the
listener; its deterministic `<ready-file>.application-ready` sibling is the
authoritative `snapback.application-ready.v1` settlement and admission
receipt.

## Preserve the sessions startup carrier

The lifecycle owner writes the complete sessions startup carrier before first
bind and rewrites it on every successful regenerate before hot-load. An
additive successor preserves the database, accounts, custody, sessions, and
client stores while advancing the complete active deployment identity. The
event stream reports the old and new identities; continuity does not mean
identity equality. `dev-fresh` is the explicit destructive verb and is never
implied by regenerate or attach.

`snapback start --startup-artifacts ...` remains available for lower-level
diagnosis and lifecycle acceptance harnesses. It is not the application
authoring path and shifts carrier correctness and process ownership to the
caller.

## Bind a separately owned client honestly

For web, `@expo/snapback-vite` managed/auto mode invokes this same fixed
profile. Configure `setup.backendDirectory` and the plugin's backend `port`;
Vite pins its own loopback port with `strictPort`, declares that client origin,
and consumes the application receipt. `virtual:snapback/dev` projects the
receipt-issued binding through the same-origin relay. It does not manufacture
binding provenance or expose the private backend origin, receipt path, or
qualified-binary facts to browser code.

The default `SnapbackExpoProvider` is supervisor-owned. A raw `{ origin }` or
raw binding override is not a supported substitute for its admitted
environment and can refuse as binding unavailable or with
`SNAPBACK_APP_BINDING_OVERRIDE_UNCONFIRMED`. For a separately owned native
Expo process, the application shell must own a complete admitted
`SnapbackExpoEnvironmentV1` (binding plus authority/custody lifecycle), or use
the lower-level app client with that admitted binding. There is currently no
safe “just pass the fixed URL” shortcut.

The supervised Expo profile declares Metro's `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, and
`localhost` loopback aliases into `runDev` before backend start. The Rust
server's consumed dev-body origin set is therefore the set written to the
receipt. Expo keeps
its device-route binding in owner-only transient `expo-supervisor.json` and the
rendezvous response; it never writes that projection back into the
application-ready file. Those are inspection/admission projections; attach
still trusts the application receipt.

## Anti-patterns

- Starting a second public lifecycle with `snapback start` for ordinary app
  authoring.
- Running `--attach` without the exact live ready descriptor and database.
- Treating port occupancy as server identity or deleting a stale listener on
  attach refusal.
- Parsing server logs instead of consuming the host and application receipts.
- Passing a raw origin to `SnapbackExpoProvider` or weakening binding
  admission after an override refusal.
- Hand-editing `startup-artifacts.json`, binding environments, or `.env*`
  origins instead of declaring the fixed profile.

name: control-in-app-browser
description: "Control the in-app Browser for opening, navigating, inspecting visible or interactive page state, clicking, typing, screenshots, and local web testing. It can have existing signed-in sessions. For semantic operations on linked resources, prefer a purpose-built connector, API, or CLI when available."
---

# Browser
## Stop: choose the right surface before any browser action
Explicit browser intent wins: if the user names the in-app browser or Chrome, or asks to open, show, or navigate to a page; inspect its visual or interactive state; or interact with its UI, continue with Browser and do not substitute a connector.

Otherwise, treat a URL or open browser tab as context, not browser intent. Earlier Browser use does not make later semantic work browser-first. Before each semantic operation on a linked resource, you MUST query available and deferred tools for an applicable connector, API, or CLI. Reading this skill or scanning visible tools does not count. Do not initialize Browser for that operation until the query is complete. Use the non-browser tool when available. If it handles the current operation, continue the larger workflow without Browser for that operation. Use Browser when no such tool exists, the tool cannot access the resource or lacks a required capability, or UI work remains; use available browser context before asking the user to repeat it.

Use this skill for browser automation tasks such as inspecting pages, navigating, testing local apps, clicking, typing, taking screenshots, and reading visible page state.

If this plugin is listed as available in the session, treat that as mandatory reading before browser work. Open and follow this skill before saying that Browser is unavailable and before falling back to standalone Playwright or Computer Use.

Do not skip this skill just because Computer Use MCP tool calls are directly visible or appear easier to invoke. The presence of Computer Use tools is not evidence that Computer Use is the preferred browser surface.

## Setup Documentation
Use `await agent.documentation.get("<name>")` when one of these setup topics applies:
- `bootstrap-troubleshooting`: read when browser setup succeeds but discovery or selection fails
- `chrome-troubleshooting`: read when Chromium browser extension setup, installation, or communication fails

## Bootstrap
These setup details are internal. User-facing progress updates should be less technical in nature. Never mention `Node REPL`, `node_repl`, `REPL`, JavaScript sessions, module exports, reading documentation, or loading instructions unless a user is asking for that exact information. If setup or recovery is needed, describe it naturally as connecting to the browser or retrying the browser connection.

The `browser-client` module is the core entry point for browser use, and is available under `scripts/browser-client.mjs` in this plugin's root directory. ALWAYS import it using an absolute path. IMPORTANT: If this path cannot be found, stop and report that this plugin is missing `scripts/browser-client.mjs`. NEVER use the built in `browser-client` library.

Run browser setup code through the Node REPL `js` tool. In this environment the callable tool id typically appears as `mcp__node_repl__js`. If it is not already available, use tool discovery for `node_repl js` without setting a result limit. You need the `js` execution tool: `js_reset` only clears state, and `js_add_node_module_dir` only changes package resolution. Do not call either helper while trying to expose `js`. If `js` is still not available, search again for `node_repl js` with `limit: 10`.

```js

```

A tab binding is separate from its browser binding. If a later turn reports that a tab is missing, stale, closed, or not part of the current browser session, discard that tab binding and obtain or create a fresh tab from the existing browser binding. Never call `agent.browsers.get*` to recover a tab; only an explicit browser-disconnected error invalidates the binding.

## Browser selection
The scenarios below are for the initial browser selection only. Before calling any `agent.browsers.get*` method, reuse an existing `globalThis.browser`, `globalThis.iab`, `globalThis.chrome`, or `globalThis.edge` binding that already serves the task. A new user turn does not invalidate a browser binding or require another selection or documentation call.

Select the initial browser with exactly one of these scenarios, in the order
shown. An explicit request for the in-app browser, Chrome, or Edge always wins
over URL selection. Never call `getForUrl()` when the user names a browser.
An explicit browser request is a hard constraint: use only that browser and
never fall back to another browser surface. If its exact selector is
unavailable, report that browser as unavailable instead of calling
`getDefault()`, `getForUrl()`, or `get("extension")`.

### The user explicitly requests a browser
A plugin mention in the user's request explicitly names its browser.
`[@Browser](plugin://browser@openai-bundled)` names the in-app browser.
Browser plugin mentions whose URL contains `browserFamily=chrome` or
`browserFamily=edge` name Chrome or Edge respectively.
`[@Chrome](plugin://chrome@openai-bundled)`,
`[@chrome-internal](plugin://chrome-internal@openai-bundled)`, and
`[@chrome-dev](plugin://chrome-dev@openai-bundled)` name Chrome. Follow the
corresponding explicit-browser scenario below.

```js
if (globalThis.iab == null) {
  globalThis.iab = await agent.browsers.get("iab");
  nodeRepl.write(await iab.documentation());
}
```

If the user explicitly requests the in-app browser but the Browser skill is not available, report that the in-app browser is unavailable instead of substituting another browser.

Chrome or Edge is available only when a Browser or Chrome skill is listed for
the session and `agent.browsers.get("chrome")` or
`agent.browsers.get("edge")` succeeds. The browser family is a stable selector;
do not list browsers first or pass an opaque browser ID for an explicit family.

documentation:

```js
if (globalThis.chrome == null) {
  globalThis.chrome = await agent.browsers.get("chrome");
  nodeRepl.write(await chrome.documentation());
}
```

documentation:

```js
if (globalThis.edge == null) {
  globalThis.edge = await agent.browsers.get("edge");
  nodeRepl.write(await edge.documentation());
}
```

tell them that browser needs the ChatGPT browser extension and direct them to
**Settings → Computer use** to install it. Do not substitute another browser.

An explicit browser choice remains in force for the task. If authentication blocks the task in an explicitly selected browser, your next response must explicitly ask the user to sign in in that browser and tell you when it is ready, unless that browser's documentation provides a supported authentication flow to try first. Merely reporting that sign-in is required is not sufficient. Do not switch to another browser unless the user asks or approves the switch.

### The user explicitly requests an external browser without naming a family
When the user says to use their external browser, browser extension, or a
similar external-browser surface without naming Chrome or Edge, select the
first connected extension instance directly. Do not call
`agent.browsers.list()` first:

```js
if (globalThis.browser == null) {
  globalThis.browser = await agent.browsers.get("extension");
  nodeRepl.write(await browser.documentation());
}
```

If no extension instance is available, tell the user that their external
browser needs the ChatGPT browser extension and direct them to
**Settings → Computer use** to install it. Do not substitute the in-app
browser.

### The task requires browser interaction, the user does not specify a browser, and the task has a target URL
When the user supplies a URL or the intended URL can be reasonably inferred from the request, replace the example below with that URL and let browser-client choose the browser best suited to it. Do not call `agent.browsers.list()` first:

```js
if (globalThis.browser == null) {
  globalThis.browser = await agent.browsers.getForUrl("https://example.com/");
  nodeRepl.write(await browser.documentation());
}
```

### The user specifies neither a browser nor a target URL
Use the runtime default, which prefers the in-app browser when it is available and otherwise uses Chrome. Do not list browsers first:

```js
if (globalThis.browser == null) {
  globalThis.browser = await agent.browsers.getDefault();
  nodeRepl.write(await browser.documentation());
}
```

## After setup
If setup succeeds but browser discovery or selection fails, read `await agent.documentation.get("bootstrap-troubleshooting")` before resetting the JavaScript session or trying another browser-control mechanism.

If the failure is specific to Chrome extension setup, installation, or communication, read `await agent.documentation.get("chrome-troubleshooting")` before retrying or taking another recovery action.

When the user did not explicitly choose a browser, a browser selected by the runtime is not a user constraint. Do not switch browsers based only on an assumption about authentication. If navigation shows that the selected browser lacks the required authentication, select another available browser before asking the user to sign in. You may select it without resetting the Node session. Preserve existing `iab`, `chrome`, `edge`, and `browser` bindings when they are still useful. Existing tabs remain bound to the browser that created them. After selecting a different browser, obtain a tab from that browser before continuing and read its complete documentation.

The ability to interact directly with browsers is exposed through the `browser-client` runtime via the `agent.browsers.*` API. Before trying to interact with a selected browser for the first time, you MUST emit and read the complete documentation returned by its `documentation()` call in one go. For the initial documentation read, run the exact direct `nodeRepl.write(await <browser>.documentation());` call shown in the applicable scenario above. Do not assign the documentation to a variable, inspect its length, slice it, truncate it, summarize it, or emit only an excerpt. Do not proactively split the documentation into pages or chunks. Only if the tool output itself explicitly reports that it was truncated may you emit and read smaller chunks until you have read the documentation in its entirety.

Only the Node REPL `js` tool (`mcp__node_repl__js`) can be used to control the selected browser. Do not use external MCP browser-control tools, separate browser automation servers, or other browser skills for this surface. References to Playwright mean the in-skill `tab.playwright` API after browser-client setup.

+# Clique build diary

+## M1 — identity, sessions, and profiles
+
+I built the sessions-mode Snapback foundation, email/password signup and login, durable browser session custody, logout, recovery-code presentation, unique handles, editable public profiles, fixture avatars, and a deliberately small authenticated home surface. The starter log is replayed in order through the same generated mutation references used by the app. The acceptance runner then checks the replayed documents and drives negative cases through the backend. The frozen two-client harness confirmed that Alice's profile edits reached Bob live, survived an Alice reload, and that logout remained logged out across another reload. An Expo iOS export also produced a Hermes bytecode bundle.
+
+The easy part was wiring the generated app identity into the Familiar provider and using the frozen UI components as the visible interaction boundary. Familiar queries and mutations read like ordinary TypeScript modules, and the generated API references made both hooks and the replay tool straightforward. That profile saved most of the conceptual translation normally spent learning a backend-specific declaration language: schema fields, indexes, arguments, return validators, queries, and mutations remained close to the Convex-shaped mental model the profile promises.
+
+The work that fought me was mostly at the edges. Moving the generated starter out of its temporary scaffold directory left runtime reservation files containing the old absolute path, so the first backend restart failed until I isolated those stale files. TypeScript 6 surfaced a stale compiler option and a query-state union needed explicit narrowing. React Native web also lacks the `Image.resolveAssetSource` shape I first assumed, which caused the first Metro render to fail until fixture asset resolution was made platform-safe. Finally, the in-app browser controller had no available browser session, so the authoritative Playwright choreography became the end-to-end diagnostic as well as the milestone proof.
+
+The Familiar profile saved boilerplate around operation definitions, generated references, validators, auth access, and React subscriptions. What remained Snapback-specific was substantial but bounded: the codegen policy, external-origin admission, runtime binding, session-storage partitioning, auth recovery behavior, table write posture, and the CLI/runtime split. One notable documentation mismatch is that the published 0.1.25 Familiar guide says `snapback/generated` is authoritative and `_generated` is retired, while the benchmark request still names `_generated/`. I followed the running binary and published codegen rather than manufacturing a second generated tree.
+
+The most useful missing diagnostic would have been an error that explicitly connected a relocated scaffold to the stale absolute runtime reservation and offered the safe cleanup target. The guide also could state more prominently that public-read tables with authenticated server mutations trigger migration-posture warnings even when the mutation itself derives the principal. A compact web-safe asset-resolution example in the Expo packet would have prevented the only browser runtime crash.
*** End Patch";

# Clique build diary

## M1 — identity, sessions, and profiles

I built the sessions-mode Snapback foundation, email/password signup and login, durable browser session custody, logout, recovery-code presentation, unique handles, editable public profiles, fixture avatars, and a deliberately small authenticated home surface. The starter log is replayed in order through the same generated mutation references used by the app. The acceptance runner then checks the replayed documents and drives negative cases through the backend. The frozen two-client harness confirmed that Alice's profile edits reached Bob live, survived an Alice reload, and that logout remained logged out across another reload. An Expo iOS export also produced a Hermes bytecode bundle.

The easy part was wiring the generated app identity into the Familiar provider and using the frozen UI components as the visible interaction boundary. Familiar queries and mutations read like ordinary TypeScript modules, and the generated API references made both hooks and the replay tool straightforward. That profile saved most of the conceptual translation normally spent learning a backend-specific declaration language: schema fields, indexes, arguments, return validators, queries, and mutations remained close to the Convex-shaped mental model the profile promises.

The work that fought me was mostly at the edges. Moving the generated starter out of its temporary scaffold directory left runtime reservation files containing the old absolute path, so the first backend restart failed until I isolated those stale files. TypeScript 6 surfaced a stale compiler option and a query-state union needed explicit narrowing. React Native web also lacks the `Image.resolveAssetSource` shape I first assumed, which caused the first Metro render to fail until fixture asset resolution was made platform-safe. Finally, the in-app browser controller had no available browser session, so the authoritative Playwright choreography became the end-to-end diagnostic as well as the milestone proof.

The Familiar profile saved boilerplate around operation definitions, generated references, validators, auth access, and React subscriptions. What remained Snapback-specific was substantial but bounded: the codegen policy, external-origin admission, runtime binding, session-storage partitioning, auth recovery behavior, table write posture, and the CLI/runtime split. One notable documentation mismatch is that the published 0.1.25 Familiar guide says `snapback/generated` is authoritative and `_generated` is retired, while the benchmark request still names `_generated/`. I followed the running binary and published codegen rather than manufacturing a second generated tree.

The most useful missing diagnostic would have been an error that explicitly connected a relocated scaffold to the stale absolute runtime reservation and offered the safe cleanup target. The guide also could state more prominently that public-read tables with authenticated server mutations trigger migration-posture warnings even when the mutation itself derives the principal. A compact web-safe asset-resolution example in the Expo packet would have prevented the only browser runtime crash.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /Users/ccheever/bench-matrix-20260823-r2/cells/sol-clique-familiar/diary.md
@@
 The most useful missing diagnostic would have been an error that explicitly connected a relocated scaffold to the stale absolute runtime reservation and offered the safe cleanup target. The guide also could state more prominently that public-read tables with authenticated server mutations trigger migration-posture warnings even when the mutation itself derives the principal. A compact web-safe asset-resolution example in the Expo packet would have prevented the only browser runtime crash.
+
+## M2 — posts, reactions, reposts, threads, and the follow graph
+
+I added the social graph and feed model as four live document sets: follow edges, posts (including direct replies), likes, and reposts. Every write derives the acting user from the authenticated context. The UI combines those subscriptions with profiles to render Global and Following projections, implicit self-membership, attributed reposts, live counts, threads, and deterministic 20-item pagination. The M2 starter replay settled all 52 new actions through those mutations. The acceptance entrypoint covered all 22 suite-owned assertions; the frozen browser harness then passed text-post delivery, follow/unfollow projection, author identity, like/unlike, repost attribution, followed-reposter projection, and live reply threads. Its two media-live checks remained the harness's declared optional skips because the frozen contract has no drivable feed media picker selector.
+
+The schema and basic mutations felt easy. Familiar indexes and the generated `v.doc`/`v.id` validators made identity-safe edges and set-state reactions concise. The client-side projection also stayed pleasantly ordinary: the live hooks supply canonical rows, while small `Set` and `Map` transforms express Global versus Following without a bespoke backend query language. The replay format was regular enough that one parser could preserve line order and fixture timestamps.
+
+What fought me was app-shell choreography. The harness deliberately carries each browser forward between assertions. A profile follow therefore needed to settle and return to a surface where feed tabs remained reachable. The own-profile component's first visible line was the frozen Edit action, while the observation expected the display name; I added an outer contracted profile surface whose first line is the name and passed a distinct test ID into the unchanged frozen component. Finally, Expo Router keeps the outgoing stack screen mounted during a push. That briefly exposed both the Global composer and thread composer under the same frozen selector, so the old composer now unmounts before the route transition. These were three correction loops around navigation state, not data liveness; the final run was green.
+
+Familiar saved the most time in the mutation layer: authenticated context, indexed reads, typed IDs, return validation, generated API references, and live hooks all remained uniform as the model expanded from one table to five. Snapback-specific constraints still shaped the result. Inline Familiar handlers cap relational `take` at 1024, generic table writes produce explicit-authority migration warnings, mutation IDs are bound to auth context, and development briefly closes app-data admission while a new schema is loading. Unique durable `sourceId` values handle fixture idempotency while each transport attempt now gets a fresh mutation ID.
+
+The codegen error for the 1024 ceiling was excellent and directly actionable. The missing diagnostic was for `SNAPBACK_AUTH_STALE_RESULT`: it should say that a replay tool must not reuse a client mutation identity under a new session even when the domain operation is idempotent. The client mutation return shape also deserves one short Familiar example; querying the settled document by its unique source ID was reliable, but the mistaken return-envelope assumption cost a loop. A guide note about Expo Router retaining an outgoing web screen during stack transitions would also help authors using globally unique test selectors.
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

import React from 'react';

export interface MessageBubbleReactionSummary {
  emoji: string;
  count: number;
  /** Whether the viewer's own reaction is this emoji. */
  mine?: boolean;
}

export interface MessageBubbleQuote {
  senderName: string;
  excerpt: string;
}

export interface MessageBubbleProps {
  /** Whether the viewer sent this message (right-aligned, accent-tinted). */
  isMine: boolean;
  /** Message text, or the caption for a media message. */
  text?: string;
  /** Media attachment URI (image URI, or video poster/thumbnail URI). */
  mediaUri?: string;
  mediaKind?: 'image' | 'video';
  /** View-once photo (brief M5). The kit never renders `mediaUri` for an opened view-once. */
  viewOnce?: boolean;
  /** Whether the viewer has already opened this view-once photo. */
  viewOnceOpened?: boolean;
  /** Sender display name (rendered for others' messages in groups). */
  senderName?: string;
  senderAvatarUri?: string;
  /** Show sender name + avatar (group conversations). Default false. */
  showSender?: boolean;
  /** Pre-formatted display timestamp (the lane formats; the kit renders). */
  timestamp?: string;
  /** "edited" label (brief M4). */
  edited?: boolean;
  /** Delete-for-everyone tombstone: renders "This message was deleted". */
  deleted?: boolean;
  /** Receipt state for the viewer's own messages. */
  receipt?: ReceiptState;
  /** Offline-queued pending state (brief M6). */
  receiptPending?: boolean;
  /** Quoted-reply excerpt (brief M3). */
  quote?: MessageBubbleQuote;
  /** Tap the quote → jump to the original message. */
  onPressQuote?: () => void;
  /** Aggregate reaction chips shown under the bubble (brief M4). */
  reactions?: readonly MessageBubbleReactionSummary[];
  /** Tap a reaction chip (reports the emoji; set/clear semantics are the lane's). */
  onPressReactionChip?: (emoji: string) => void;
  /** Tap the media (open viewer / play video / open view-once). */
  onPressMedia?: () => void;
  /** Long-press the bubble (lanes typically open the reaction picker / actions). */
  onLongPress?: () => void;
  /** Tap a detected http(s) link in the text (e.g. Linking.openURL). */
  onPressLink?: (url: string) => void;
  /** Per-chat accent color; tints the viewer's own bubbles. */
  accentColor?: string;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-bubble`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function mediaBlock(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const { mediaUri, mediaKind, viewOnce, viewOnceOpened, onPressMedia } = props;
  if (viewOnce) {
    // View-once media is never rendered inline; only an open/opened affordance.
    return (
      <Pressable
        accessibilityLabel={viewOnceOpened ? 'View-once photo, already opened' : 'View-once photo'}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        disabled={!!viewOnceOpened}
        onPress={onPressMedia}
        style={styles.viewOnce}
        testID="sm-convo-viewonce"
      >
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceIcon}>{viewOnceOpened ? '◌' : '①'}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceLabel}>
          {viewOnceOpened ? 'Opened' : 'Photo — view once'}
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    );
  }
  if (!mediaUri && mediaKind !== 'video') {
    return null;
  }
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityLabel={mediaKind === 'video' ? 'Video message' : 'Photo message'}
      accessibilityRole="imagebutton"
      onPress={onPressMedia}
      style={styles.media}
      testID="sm-convo-media"
    >
      {mediaUri ? (
        <Image source={{ uri: mediaUri }} style={styles.mediaImage} />
      ) : (
        <View style={[styles.mediaImage, styles.mediaPlaceholder]} />
      )}
      {mediaKind === 'video' ? (
        <View pointerEvents="none" style={styles.playOverlay}>
          <Text style={styles.playGlyph}>▶</Text>
        </View>
      ) : null}
    </Pressable>
  );
}

/**
 * One chat message bubble (brief M3–M6): text and media, quoted replies,
 * edited/tombstone states, receipt ticks, reaction chips, view-once
 * affordance. Purely presentational; every behavior is a callback.
 */
export function MessageBubble(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element {
  const {
    isMine,
    text,
    senderName,
    senderAvatarUri,
    showSender = false,
    timestamp,
    edited = false,
    deleted = false,
    receipt,
    receiptPending = false,
    quote,
    onPressQuote,
    reactions,
    onPressReactionChip,
    onLongPress,
    onPressLink,
    accentColor,
    testID = 'sm-convo-bubble',
  } = props;

  const bubbleColor = isMine
    ? accentColor
      ? `${accentColor}26` // pinned accents are 6-digit hex; 26 ≈ 15% alpha tint
      : palette.bubbleMine
    : palette.bubbleTheirs;

  return (
    <View style={[styles.row, isMine ? styles.rowMine : styles.rowTheirs]}>
      {!isMine && showSender ? (
        <View style={styles.avatarSlot}>
          <Avatar label={senderName ?? '?'} size={28} {...(senderAvatarUri ? { uri: senderAvatarUri } : {})} />
        </View>
      ) : null}
      <View style={styles.stack}>
        <Pressable
          accessibilityLabel={
            deleted ? 'Deleted message' : `Message${senderName ? ` from ${senderName}` : ''}`
          }
          onLongPress={onLongPress}
          style={[styles.bubble, { backgroundColor: bubbleColor }]}
          testID={testID}
        >
          {!isMine && showSender && senderName ? (
            <Text style={[styles.sender, accentColor ? { color: accentColor } : null]}>
              {senderName}
            </Text>
          ) : null}
          {quote ? (
            <QuotedReply
              excerpt={quote.excerpt}
              senderName={quote.senderName}
              {...(accentColor ? { accentColor } : {})}
              {...(onPressQuote ? { onPress: onPressQuote } : {})}
            />
          ) : null}
          {deleted ? (
            <Text style={styles.tombstone} testID="sm-convo-tombstone">
              This message was deleted
            </Text>
          ) : (
            <>
              {mediaBlock(props)}
              {text ? (
                <Text style={styles.text}>{renderLinkifiedText(text, onPressLink)}</Text>
              ) : null}
            </>
          )}
          <View style={styles.footer}>
            {edited && !deleted ? <Text style={styles.edited}>edited</Text> : null}
            {timestamp ? <Text style={styles.timestamp}>{timestamp}</Text> : null}
            {isMine && !deleted && (receipt || receiptPending) ? (
              <ReceiptTicks pending={receiptPending} state={receipt ?? 'sent'} />
            ) : null}
          </View>
        </Pressable>
        {reactions && reactions.length > 0 ? (
          <View style={[styles.reactions, isMine ? styles.reactionsMine : null]}>
            {reactions.map((r) => (
              <Pressable
                accessibilityLabel={`${r.emoji} ${r.count}${r.mine ? ', including you' : ''}`}
                accessibilityRole="button"
                accessibilityState={{ selected: !!r.mine }}
                key={r.emoji}
                onPress={onPressReactionChip ? () => onPressReactionChip(r.emoji) : undefined}
                style={[styles.reactionChip, r.mine ? styles.reactionChipMine : null]}
                testID="sm-convo-reaction-chip"
              >
                <Text style={styles.reactionText}>
                  {r.emoji} {r.count}
                </Text>
              </Pressable>
            ))}
          </View>
        ) : null}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { Animated, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
import { palette, radii, spacing, typeScale } from './tokens';

export interface TypingIndicatorProps {
  /** Whether anyone is typing. When false the component renders nothing. */
  visible: boolean;
  /** Display names of who is typing (used for the accessibility label). */
  names?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Compact variant: a one-line "typing…" text hint (for the chats list).
   * Default is the in-conversation "…" bubble.
   */
  compact?: boolean;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-typing`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function typingLabel(names: readonly string[] | undefined): string {
  if (!names || names.length === 0) {
    return 'typing';
  }
  if (names.length === 1) {
    return `${names[0]} is typing`;
  }
  return `${names.join(', ')} are typing`;
}

/**
 * The "…" typing hint (brief M3): shown in the conversation as a pulsing
 * three-dot bubble, and in the chats list as a compact text hint.
 * Purely presentational — visibility, timing windows, and expiry are the
 * lane's job.
 */
export function TypingIndicator({
  visible,
  names,
  compact = false,
  testID = 'sm-convo-typing',
}: TypingIndicatorProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const pulse = useRef(new Animated.Value(0.4)).current;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!visible) {
      return;
    }
    const loop = Animated.loop(
      Animated.sequence([
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 1, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 0.4, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
      ]),
    );
    loop.start();
    return () => loop.stop();
  }, [visible, pulse]);

  if (!visible) {
    return null;
  }

  const label = typingLabel(names);

  if (compact) {
    return (
      <Text
        accessibilityLabel={label}
        style={styles.compact}
        testID={testID}
      >
        typing…
      </Text>
    );
  }

  return (
    <View accessibilityLabel={label} style={styles.bubble} testID={testID}>
      <Animated.Text style={[styles.dots, { opacity: pulse }]}>…</Animated.Text>
    </View>
  );
}

import React from 'react';
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
import { palette, radii, spacing, typeScale } from './tokens';

export interface QuotedReplyProps {
  /** Display name of the quoted message's sender. */
  senderName: string;
  /** Pre-truncated excerpt of the quoted message (the lane decides length). */
  excerpt: string;
  /** Accent bar color (per-chat accent). */
  accentColor?: string;
  /** Tap → jump/scroll to the original message (the lane implements the jump). */
  onPress?: () => void;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-quote-preview`. */
  testID?: string;
}

/**
 * WhatsApp-style quoted-reply excerpt block (brief M3): rendered inside or
 * above a message bubble; tapping jumps to the original.
 */
export function QuotedReply({
  senderName,
  excerpt,
  accentColor = palette.primary,
  onPress,
  testID = 'sm-convo-quote-preview',
}: QuotedReplyProps): React.JSX.Element {
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityLabel={`Quoted reply to ${senderName}: ${excerpt}`}
      accessibilityRole="button"
      onPress={onPress}
      style={styles.container}
      testID={testID}
    >
      <View style={[styles.bar, { backgroundColor: accentColor }]} />
      <View style={styles.body}>
        <Text numberOfLines={1} style={[styles.sender, { color: accentColor }]}>
          {senderName}
        </Text>
        <Text numberOfLines={2} style={styles.excerpt}>
          {excerpt}
        </Text>
      </View>
    </Pressable>
  );
}

import React from 'react';
import { Image, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
import { Avatar } from './Avatar';
import { QuotedReply } from './QuotedReply';
import { ReceiptTicks, ReceiptState } from './ReceiptTicks';
import { renderLinkifiedText } from './linkify';
import { palette, radii, spacing, typeScale } from './tokens';

export interface MessageBubbleReactionSummary {
  emoji: string;
  count: number;
  /** Whether the viewer's own reaction is this emoji. */
  mine?: boolean;
}

export interface MessageBubbleQuote {
  senderName: string;
  excerpt: string;
}

export interface MessageBubbleProps {
  /** Whether the viewer sent this message (right-aligned, accent-tinted). */
  isMine: boolean;
  /** Message text, or the caption for a media message. */
  text?: string;
  /** Media attachment URI (image URI, or video poster/thumbnail URI). */
  mediaUri?: string;
  mediaKind?: 'image' | 'video';
  /** View-once photo (brief M5). The kit never renders `mediaUri` for an opened view-once. */
  viewOnce?: boolean;
  /** Whether the viewer has already opened this view-once photo. */
  viewOnceOpened?: boolean;
  /** Sender display name (rendered for others' messages in groups). */
  senderName?: string;
  senderAvatarUri?: string;
  /** Show sender name + avatar (group conversations). Default false. */
  showSender?: boolean;
  /** Pre-formatted display timestamp (the lane formats; the kit renders). */
  timestamp?: string;
  /** "edited" label (brief M4). */
  edited?: boolean;
  /** Delete-for-everyone tombstone: renders "This message was deleted". */
  deleted?: boolean;
  /** Receipt state for the viewer's own messages. */
  receipt?: ReceiptState;
  /** Offline-queued pending state (brief M6). */
  receiptPending?: boolean;
  /** Quoted-reply excerpt (brief M3). */
  quote?: MessageBubbleQuote;
  /** Tap the quote → jump to the original message. */
  onPressQuote?: () => void;
  /** Aggregate reaction chips shown under the bubble (brief M4). */
  reactions?: readonly MessageBubbleReactionSummary[];
  /** Tap a reaction chip (reports the emoji; set/clear semantics are the lane's). */
  onPressReactionChip?: (emoji: string) => void;
  /** Tap the media (open viewer / play video / open view-once). */
  onPressMedia?: () => void;
  /** Long-press the bubble (lanes typically open the reaction picker / actions). */
  onLongPress?: () => void;
  /** Tap a detected http(s) link in the text (e.g. Linking.openURL). */
  onPressLink?: (url: string) => void;
  /** Per-chat accent color; tints the viewer's own bubbles. */
  accentColor?: string;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-bubble`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function mediaBlock(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const { mediaUri, mediaKind, viewOnce, viewOnceOpened, onPressMedia } = props;
  if (viewOnce) {
    // View-once media is never rendered inline; only an open/opened affordance.
    return (
      <Pressable
        accessibilityLabel={viewOnceOpened ? 'View-once photo, already opened' : 'View-once photo'}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        disabled={!!viewOnceOpened}
        onPress={onPressMedia}
        style={styles.viewOnce}
        testID="sm-convo-viewonce"
      >
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceIcon}>{viewOnceOpened ? '◌' : '①'}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceLabel}>
          {viewOnceOpened ? 'Opened' : 'Photo — view once'}
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    );
  }
  if (!mediaUri && mediaKind !== 'video') {
    return null;
  }
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityLabel={mediaKind === 'video' ? 'Video message' : 'Photo message'}
      accessibilityRole="imagebutton"
      onPress={onPressMedia}
      style={styles.media}
      testID="sm-convo-media"
    >
      {mediaUri ? (
        <Image source={{ uri: mediaUri }} style={styles.mediaImage} />
      ) : (
        <View style={[styles.mediaImage, styles.mediaPlaceholder]} />
      )}
      {mediaKind === 'video' ? (
        <View pointerEvents="none" style={styles.playOverlay}>
          <Text style={styles.playGlyph}>▶</Text>
        </View>
      ) : null}
    </Pressable>
  );
}

/**
 * One chat message bubble (brief M3–M6): text and media, quoted replies,
 * edited/tombstone states, receipt ticks, reaction chips, view-once
 * affordance. Purely presentational; every behavior is a callback.
 */
export function MessageBubble(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element {
  const {
    isMine,
    text,
    senderName,
    senderAvatarUri,
    showSender = false,
    timestamp,
    edited = false,
    deleted = false,
    receipt,
    receiptPending = false,
    quote,
    onPressQuote,
    reactions,
    onPressReactionChip,
    onLongPress,
    onPressLink,
    accentColor,
    testID = 'sm-convo-bubble',
  } = props;

  const bubbleColor = isMine
    ? accentColor
      ? `${accentColor}26` // pinned accents are 6-digit hex; 26 ≈ 15% alpha tint
      : palette.bubbleMine
    : palette.bubbleTheirs;

  return (
    <View style={[styles.row, isMine ? styles.rowMine : styles.rowTheirs]}>
      {!isMine && showSender ? (
        <View style={styles.avatarSlot}>
          <Avatar label={senderName ?? '?'} size={28} {...(senderAvatarUri ? { uri: senderAvatarUri } : {})} />
        </View>
      ) : null}
      <View style={styles.stack}>
        <Pressable
          accessibilityLabel={
            deleted ? 'Deleted message' : `Message${senderName ? ` from ${senderName}` : ''}`
          }
          onLongPress={onLongPress}
          style={[styles.bubble, { backgroundColor: bubbleColor }]}
          testID={testID}
        >
          {!isMine && showSender && senderName ? (
            <Text style={[styles.sender, accentColor ? { color: accentColor } : null]}>
              {senderName}
            </Text>
          ) : null}
          {quote ? (
            <QuotedReply
              excerpt={quote.excerpt}
              senderName={quote.senderName}
              {...(accentColor ? { accentColor } : {})}
              {...(onPressQuote ? { onPress: onPressQuote } : {})}
            />
          ) : null}
          {deleted ? (
            <Text style={styles.tombstone} testID="sm-convo-tombstone">
              This message was deleted
            </Text>
          ) : (
            <>
              {mediaBlock(props)}
              {text ? (
                <Text style={styles.text}>{renderLinkifiedText(text, onPressLink)}</Text>
              ) : null}
            </>
          )}
          <View style={styles.footer}>
            {edited && !deleted ? <Text style={styles.edited}>edited</Text> : null}
            {timestamp ? <Text style={styles.timestamp}>{timestamp}</Text> : null}
            {isMine && !deleted && (receipt || receiptPending) ? (
              <ReceiptTicks pending={receiptPending} state={receipt ?? 'sent'} />
            ) : null}
          </View>
        </Pressable>
        {reactions && reactions.length > 0 ? (
          <View style={[styles.reactions, isMine ? styles.reactionsMine : null]}>
            {reactions.map((r) => (
              <Pressable
                accessibilityLabel={`${r.emoji} ${r.count}${r.mine ? ', including you' : ''}`}
                accessibilityRole="button"
                accessibilityState={{ selected: !!r.mine }}
                key={r.emoji}
                onPress={onPressReactionChip ? () => onPressReactionChip(r.emoji) : undefined}
                style={[styles.reactionChip, r.mine ? styles.reactionChipMine : null]}
                testID="sm-convo-reaction-chip"
              >
                <Text style={styles.reactionText}>
                  {r.emoji} {r.count}
                </Text>
              </Pressable>
            ))}
          </View>
        ) : null}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: {

import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { Animated, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
import { palette, radii, spacing, typeScale } from './tokens';

export interface TypingIndicatorProps {
  /** Whether anyone is typing. When false the component renders nothing. */
  visible: boolean;
  /** Display names of who is typing (used for the accessibility label). */
  names?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Compact variant: a one-line "typing…" text hint (for the chats list).
   * Default is the in-conversation "…" bubble.
   */
  compact?: boolean;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-typing`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function typingLabel(names: readonly string[] | undefined): string {
  if (!names || names.length === 0) {
    return 'typing';
  }
  if (names.length === 1) {
    return `${names[0]} is typing`;
  }
  return `${names.join(', ')} are typing`;
}

/**
 * The "…" typing hint (brief M3): shown in the conversation as a pulsing
 * three-dot bubble, and in the chats list as a compact text hint.
 * Purely presentational — visibility, timing windows, and expiry are the
 * lane's job.
 */
export function TypingIndicator({
  visible,
  names,
  compact = false,
  testID = 'sm-convo-typing',
}: TypingIndicatorProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const pulse = useRef(new Animated.Value(0.4)).current;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!visible) {
      return;
    }
    const loop = Animated.loop(
      Animated.sequence([
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 1, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 0.4, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
      ]),
    );
    loop.start();
    return () => loop.stop();
  }, [visible, pulse]);

  if (!visible) {
    return null;
  }

  const label = typingLabel(names);

  if (compact) {
    return (
      <Text
        accessibilityLabel={label}
        style={styles.compact}
        testID={testID}
      >
        typing…
      </Text>
    );
  }

  return (
    <View accessibilityLabel={label} style={styles.bubble} testID={testID}>
      <Animated.Text style={[styles.dots, { opacity: pulse }]}>…</Animated.Text>
    </View>
  );
}

import React from 'react';
import { Image, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
import { Avatar } from './Avatar';
import { QuotedReply } from './QuotedReply';
import { ReceiptTicks, ReceiptState } from './ReceiptTicks';

export interface MessageBubbleReactionSummary {
  emoji: string;
  count: number;
  /** Whether the viewer's own reaction is this emoji. */
  mine?: boolean;
}

export interface MessageBubbleQuote {
  senderName: string;
  excerpt: string;
}

export interface MessageBubbleProps {
  /** Whether the viewer sent this message (right-aligned, accent-tinted). */
  isMine: boolean;
  /** Message text, or the caption for a media message. */
  text?: string;
  /** Media attachment URI (image URI, or video poster/thumbnail URI). */
  mediaUri?: string;
  mediaKind?: 'image' | 'video';
  /** View-once photo (brief M5). The kit never renders `mediaUri` for an opened view-once. */
  viewOnce?: boolean;
  /** Whether the viewer has already opened this view-once photo. */
  viewOnceOpened?: boolean;
  /** Sender display name (rendered for others' messages in groups). */
  senderName?: string;
  senderAvatarUri?: string;
  /** Show sender name + avatar (group conversations). Default false. */
  showSender?: boolean;
  /** Pre-formatted display timestamp (the lane formats; the kit renders). */
  timestamp?: string;
  /** "edited" label (brief M4). */
  edited?: boolean;
  /** Delete-for-everyone tombstone: renders "This message was deleted". */
  deleted?: boolean;
  /** Receipt state for the viewer's own messages. */
  receipt?: ReceiptState;
  /** Offline-queued pending state (brief M6). */
  receiptPending?: boolean;
  /** Quoted-reply excerpt (brief M3). */
  quote?: MessageBubbleQuote;
  /** Tap the quote → jump to the original message. */
  onPressQuote?: () => void;
  /** Aggregate reaction chips shown under the bubble (brief M4). */
  reactions?: readonly MessageBubbleReactionSummary[];
  /** Tap a reaction chip (reports the emoji; set/clear semantics are the lane's). */
  onPressReactionChip?: (emoji: string) => void;
  /** Tap the media (open viewer / play video / open view-once). */
  onPressMedia?: () => void;
  /** Long-press the bubble (lanes typically open the reaction picker / actions). */
  onLongPress?: () => void;
  /** Tap a detected http(s) link in the text (e.g. Linking.openURL). */
  onPressLink?: (url: string) => void;
  /** Per-chat accent color; tints the viewer's own bubbles. */
  accentColor?: string;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-bubble`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function mediaBlock(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const { mediaUri, mediaKind, viewOnce, viewOnceOpened, onPressMedia } = props;
  if (viewOnce) {
    // View-once media is never rendered inline; only an open/opened affordance.
    return (
      <Pressable
        accessibilityLabel={viewOnceOpened ? 'View-once photo, already opened' : 'View-once photo'}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        disabled={!!viewOnceOpened}
        onPress={onPressMedia}
        style={styles.viewOnce}
        testID="sm-convo-viewonce"
      >
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceIcon}>{viewOnceOpened ? '◌' : '①'}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceLabel}>
          {viewOnceOpened ? 'Opened' : 'Photo — view once'}
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    );
  }
  if (!mediaUri && mediaKind !== 'video') {
    return null;
  }
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityLabel={mediaKind === 'video' ? 'Video message' : 'Photo message'}
      accessibilityRole="imagebutton"
      onPress={onPressMedia}
      style={styles.media}
      testID="sm-convo-media"
    >
      {mediaUri ? (
        <Image source={{ uri: mediaUri }} style={styles.mediaImage} />
      ) : (
        <View style={[styles.mediaImage, styles.mediaPlaceholder]} />
      )}
      {mediaKind === 'video' ? (
        <View pointerEvents="none" style={styles.playOverlay}>
          <Text style={styles.playGlyph}>▶</Text>
        </View>
      ) : null}
    </Pressable>
  );
}

/**
 * One chat message bubble (brief M3–M6): text and media, quoted replies,
 * edited/tombstone states, receipt ticks, reaction chips, view-once
 * affordance. Purely presentational; every behavior is a callback.
 */
export function MessageBubble(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element {
  const {
    isMine,
    text,
    senderName,
    senderAvatarUri,
    showSender = false,
    timestamp,
    edited = false,
    deleted = false,
    receipt,
    receiptPending = false,
    quote,
    onPressQuote,
    reactions,
    onPressReactionChip,
    onLongPress,
    onPressLink,
    accentColor,
    testID = 'sm-convo-bubble',
  } = props;

  const bubbleColor = isMine
    ? accentColor
      ? `${accentColor}26` // pinned accents are 6-digit hex; 26 ≈ 15% alpha tint
      : palette.bubbleMine
    : palette.bubbleTheirs;

  return (
    <View style={[styles.row, isMine ? styles.rowMine : styles.rowTheirs]}>
      {!isMine && showSender ? (
        <View style={styles.avatarSlot}>
          <Avatar label={senderName ?? '?'} size={28} {...(senderAvatarUri ? { uri: senderAvatarUri } : {})} />
        </View>
      ) : null}
      <View style={styles.stack}>
        <Pressable
          accessibilityLabel={
            deleted ? 'Deleted message' : `Message${senderName ? ` from ${senderName}` : ''}`
          }
          onLongPress={onLongPress}
          style={[styles.bubble, { backgroundColor: bubbleColor }]}
          testID={testID}
        >
          {!isMine && showSender && senderName ? (
            <Text style={[styles.sender, accentColor ? { color: accentColor } : null]}>
              {senderName}
            </Text>
          ) : null}
          {quote ? (
            <QuotedReply
              excerpt={quote.excerpt}
              senderName={quote.senderName}
              {...(accentColor ? { accentColor } : {})}
              {...(onPressQuote ? { onPress: onPressQuote } : {})}
            />
          ) : null}
          {deleted ? (
            <Text style={styles.tombstone} testID="sm-convo-tombstone">
              This message was deleted
            </Text>
          ) : (
            <>
              {mediaBlock(props)}
              {text ? (
                <Text style={styles.text}>{renderLinkifiedText(text, onPressLink)}</Text>
              ) : null}
            </>
          )}
          <View style={styles.footer}>
            {edited && !deleted ? <Text style={styles.edited}>edited</Text> : null}
            {timestamp ? <Text style={styles.timestamp}>{timestamp}</Text> : null}
            {isMine && !deleted && (receipt || receiptPending) ? (
              <ReceiptTicks pending={receiptPending} state={receipt ?? 'sent'} />
            ) : null}
          </View>
        </Pressable>
        {reactions && reactions.length > 0 ? (
          <View style={[styles.reactions, isMine ? styles.reactionsMine : null]}>
            {reactions.map((r) => (
              <Pressable
                accessibilityLabel={`${r.emoji} ${r.count}${r.mine ? ', including you' : ''}`}
                accessibilityRole="button"
                accessibilityState={{ selected: !!r.mine }}
                key={r.emoji}
                onPress={onPressReactionChip ? () => onPressReactionChip(r.emoji) : undefined}
                style={[styles.reactionChip, r.mine ? styles.reactionChipMine : null]}
                testID="sm-convo-reaction-chip"
              >
                <Text style={styles.reactionText}>
                  {r.emoji} {r.count}
                </Text>
              </Pressable>
            ))}
          </View>
        ) : null}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

export interface TypingIndicatorProps {
  /** Whether anyone is typing. When false the component renders nothing. */
  visible: boolean;
  /** Display names of who is typing (used for the accessibility label). */
  names?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Compact variant: a one-line "typing…" text hint (for the chats list).
   * Default is the in-conversation "…" bubble.
   */
  compact?: boolean;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-typing`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function typingLabel(names: readonly string[] | undefined): string {
  if (!names || names.length === 0) {
    return 'typing';
  }
  if (names.length === 1) {
    return `${names[0]} is typing`;
  }
  return `${names.join(', ')} are typing`;
}

/**
 * The "…" typing hint (brief M3): shown in the conversation as a pulsing
 * three-dot bubble, and in the chats list as a compact text hint.
 * Purely presentational — visibility, timing windows, and expiry are the
 * lane's job.
 */
export function TypingIndicator({
  visible,
  names,
  compact = false,
  testID = 'sm-convo-typing',
}: TypingIndicatorProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const pulse = useRef(new Animated.Value(0.4)).current;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!visible) {
      return;
    }
    const loop = Animated.loop(
      Animated.sequence([
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 1, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 0.4, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
      ]),
    );
    loop.start();
    return () => loop.stop();
  }, [visible, pulse]);

  if (!visible) {
    return null;
  }

  const label = typingLabel(names);

  if (compact) {
    return (
      <Text
        accessibilityLabel={label}
        style={styles.compact}
        testID={testID}
      >
        typing…
      </Text>
    );
  }

  return (
    <View accessibilityLabel={label} style={styles.bubble} testID={testID}>
      <Animated.Text style={[styles.dots, { opacity: pulse }]}>…</Animated.Text>
    </View>
  );
}

import React from 'react';
import { Image, Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';
import { Avatar } from './Avatar';
import { QuotedReply } from './QuotedReply';
import { ReceiptTicks, ReceiptState } from './ReceiptTicks';
import { renderLinkifiedText } from './linkify';
import { palette, radii, spacing, typeScale } from './tokens';

export interface MessageBubbleReactionSummary {
  emoji: string;
  count: number;
  /** Whether the viewer's own reaction is this emoji. */
  mine?: boolean;
}

export interface MessageBubbleQuote {
  senderName: string;
  excerpt: string;
}

export interface MessageBubbleProps {
  /** Whether the viewer sent this message (right-aligned, accent-tinted). */
  isMine: boolean;
  /** Message text, or the caption for a media message. */
  text?: string;
  /** Media attachment URI (image URI, or video poster/thumbnail URI). */
  mediaUri?: string;
  mediaKind?: 'image' | 'video';
  /** View-once photo (brief M5). The kit never renders `mediaUri` for an opened view-once. */
  viewOnce?: boolean;
  /** Whether the viewer has already opened this view-once photo. */
  viewOnceOpened?: boolean;
  /** Sender display name (rendered for others' messages in groups). */
  senderName?: string;
  senderAvatarUri?: string;
  /** Show sender name + avatar (group conversations). Default false. */
  showSender?: boolean;
  /** Pre-formatted display timestamp (the lane formats; the kit renders). */
  timestamp?: string;
  /** "edited" label (brief M4). */
  edited?: boolean;
  /** Delete-for-everyone tombstone: renders "This message was deleted". */
  deleted?: boolean;
  /** Receipt state for the viewer's own messages. */
  receipt?: ReceiptState;
  /** Offline-queued pending state (brief M6). */
  receiptPending?: boolean;
  /** Quoted-reply excerpt (brief M3). */
  quote?: MessageBubbleQuote;
  /** Tap the quote → jump to the original message. */
  onPressQuote?: () => void;
  /** Aggregate reaction chips shown under the bubble (brief M4). */
  reactions?: readonly MessageBubbleReactionSummary[];
  /** Tap a reaction chip (reports the emoji; set/clear semantics are the lane's). */
  onPressReactionChip?: (emoji: string) => void;
  /** Tap the media (open viewer / play video / open view-once). */
  onPressMedia?: () => void;
  /** Long-press the bubble (lanes typically open the reaction picker / actions). */
  onLongPress?: () => void;
  /** Tap a detected http(s) link in the text (e.g. Linking.openURL). */
  onPressLink?: (url: string) => void;
  /** Per-chat accent color; tints the viewer's own bubbles. */
  accentColor?: string;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-bubble`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function mediaBlock(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const { mediaUri, mediaKind, viewOnce, viewOnceOpened, onPressMedia } = props;
  if (viewOnce) {
    // View-once media is never rendered inline; only an open/opened affordance.
    return (
      <Pressable
        accessibilityLabel={viewOnceOpened ? 'View-once photo, already opened' : 'View-once photo'}
        accessibilityRole="button"
        disabled={!!viewOnceOpened}
        onPress={onPressMedia}
        style={styles.viewOnce}
        testID="sm-convo-viewonce"
      >
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceIcon}>{viewOnceOpened ? '◌' : '①'}</Text>
        <Text style={styles.viewOnceLabel}>
          {viewOnceOpened ? 'Opened' : 'Photo — view once'}
        </Text>
      </Pressable>
    );
  }
  if (!mediaUri && mediaKind !== 'video') {
    return null;
  }
  return (
    <Pressable
      accessibilityLabel={mediaKind === 'video' ? 'Video message' : 'Photo message'}
      accessibilityRole="imagebutton"
      onPress={onPressMedia}
      style={styles.media}
      testID="sm-convo-media"
    >
      {mediaUri ? (
        <Image source={{ uri: mediaUri }} style={styles.mediaImage} />
      ) : (
        <View style={[styles.mediaImage, styles.mediaPlaceholder]} />
      )}
      {mediaKind === 'video' ? (
        <View pointerEvents="none" style={styles.playOverlay}>
          <Text style={styles.playGlyph}>▶</Text>
        </View>
      ) : null}
    </Pressable>
  );
}

/**
 * One chat message bubble (brief M3–M6): text and media, quoted replies,
 * edited/tombstone states, receipt ticks, reaction chips, view-once
 * affordance. Purely presentational; every behavior is a callback.
 */
export function MessageBubble(props: MessageBubbleProps): React.JSX.Element {
  const {
    isMine,
    text,
    senderName,
    senderAvatarUri,
    showSender = false,
    timestamp,
    edited = false,
    deleted = false,
    receipt,
    receiptPending = false,
    quote,
    onPressQuote,
    reactions,
    onPressReactionChip,
    onLongPress,
    onPressLink,
    accentColor,
    testID = 'sm-convo-bubble',
  } = props;

  const bubbleColor = isMine
    ? accentColor
      ? `${accentColor}26` // pinned accents are 6-digit hex; 26 ≈ 15% alpha tint
      : palette.bubbleMine
    : palette.bubbleTheirs;

  return (
    <View style={[styles.row, isMine ? styles.rowMine : styles.rowTheirs]}>
      {!isMine && showSender ? (
        <View style={styles.avatarSlot}>
          <Avatar label={senderName ?? '?'} size={28} {...(senderAvatarUri ? { uri: senderAvatarUri } : {})} />
        </View>
      ) : null}
      <View style={styles.stack}>
        <Pressable
          accessibilityLabel={
            deleted ? 'Deleted message' : `Message${senderName ? ` from ${senderName}` : ''}`
          }
          onLongPress={onLongPress}
          style={[styles.bubble, { backgroundColor: bubbleColor }]}
          testID={testID}
        >
          {!isMine && showSender && senderName ? (
            <Text style={[styles.sender, accentColor ? { color: accentColor } : null]}>
              {senderName}
            </Text>
          ) : null}
          {quote ? (
            <QuotedReply
              excerpt={quote.excerpt}
              senderName={quote.senderName}
              {...(accentColor ? { accentColor } : {})}
              {...(onPressQuote ? { onPress: onPressQuote } : {})}
            />
          ) : null}
          {deleted ? (
            <Text style={styles.tombstone} testID="sm-convo-tombstone">
              This message was deleted
            </Text>
          ) : (
            <>
              {mediaBlock(props)}
              {text ? (
                <Text style={styles.text}>{renderLinkifiedText(text, onPressLink)}</Text>
              ) : null}
            </>
          )}
          <View style={styles.footer}>
            {edited && !deleted ? <Text style={styles.edited}>edited</Text> : null}
            {timestamp ? <Text style={styles.timestamp}>{timestamp}</Text> : null}
            {isMine && !deleted && (receipt || receiptPending) ? (
              <ReceiptTicks pending={receiptPending} state={receipt ?? 'sent'} />
            ) : null}
          </View>
        </Pressable>
        {reactions && reactions.length > 0 ? (
          <View style={[styles.reactions, isMine ? styles.reactionsMine : null]}>
            {reactions.map((r) => (
              <Pressable
                accessibilityLabel={`${r.emoji} ${r.count}${r.mine ? ', including you' : ''}`}
                accessibilityRole="button"
                accessibilityState={{ selected: !!r.mine }}
                key={r.emoji}
                onPress={onPressReactionChip ? () => onPressReactionChip(r.emoji) : undefined}
                style={[styles.reactionChip, r.mine ? styles.reactionChipMine : null]}
                testID="sm-convo-reaction-chip"
              >
                <Text style={styles.reactionText}>
                  {r.emoji} {r.count}
                </Text>
              </Pressable>
            ))}
          </View>
        ) : null}
      </View>
    </View>
  );
}

export interface TypingIndicatorProps {
  /** Whether anyone is typing. When false the component renders nothing. */
  visible: boolean;
  /** Display names of who is typing (used for the accessibility label). */
  names?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * Compact variant: a one-line "typing…" text hint (for the chats list).

   */
  compact?: boolean;
  /** Contract testID. Default `sm-convo-typing`. */
  testID?: string;
}

function typingLabel(names: readonly string[] | undefined): string {
  if (!names || names.length === 0) {
    return 'typing';
  }
  if (names.length === 1) {
    return `${names[0]} is typing`;
  }
  return `${names.join(', ')} are typing`;
}

/**
 * The "…" typing hint (brief M3): shown in the conversation as a pulsing
 * three-dot bubble, and in the chats list as a compact text hint.
 * Purely presentational — visibility, timing windows, and expiry are the
 * lane's job.
 */
export function TypingIndicator({
  visible,
  names,
  compact = false,
  testID = 'sm-convo-typing',
}: TypingIndicatorProps): React.JSX.Element | null {
  const pulse = useRef(new Animated.Value(0.4)).current;

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!visible) {
      return;
    }
    const loop = Animated.loop(
      Animated.sequence([
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 1, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
        Animated.timing(pulse, { toValue: 0.4, duration: 500, useNativeDriver: false }),
      ]),
    );
    loop.start();
    return () => loop.stop();
  }, [visible, pulse]);

  if (!visible) {
    return null;
  }

  const label = typingLabel(names);

  if (compact) {
    return (
      <Text
        accessibilityLabel={label}
        style={styles.compact}
        testID={testID}
      >
        typing…
      </Text>
    );
  }

  return (
    <View accessibilityLabel={label} style={styles.bubble} testID={testID}>
      <Animated.Text style={[styles.dots, { opacity: pulse }]}>…</Animated.Text>
    </View>
  );
}
